h1: Site Office Container for Live Construction Projects
seoTitle: Site Office Container Price, Sizes and GA Layouts | SAMAN
metaDescription: Six approved site office container sizes from 160 to 480 sq ft, priced from Rs 2,37,600 ex GST, with signed GA plans, workstation counts and honest site scope.
opener:
A site office container is the room your project runs from. Engineers mark up drawings there, the contractor signs the day's work, and clients sit down without walking the slab. SAMAN builds it as a welded steel box on a 125 x 75 x 4 mm base channel, clad in corrugated sheet. So it survives being lifted and moved as the work front shifts. Six approved sizes run from 160 to 480 sq ft.

Each one carries a signed general arrangement plan, so you know the door and window positions and the exact workstation count before you order. The two 40 ft wide layouts add a manager cabin behind a partition. Prices below are ex GST and cover the finished cabin.
materialLabel: 125 x 75 x 4 mm MS C-channel base, corrugated MS shell
priceCaption: Ex GST prices. GST at 18 per cent extra.

variants.shortDescription: At 160 sq ft this is the smallest office SAMAN will sign a GA plan for. Three workstations sit along the rear wall, each with a chair and an overhead file cabinet. The aisle down the middle stays clear, so nobody squeezes past a drawing table. One door on the front wall keeps entry controlled at a single point. Six windows give cross light. At 8 ft of width there is no room for a second desk run. Treat three seats as the honest limit.

variants.shortDescription: Two extra feet of width change the plan completely. Five workstations now fit, three along the rear wall and two along the front, and the aisle still runs clear between them. This is the size most Indian site teams settle on for a mid-size project. It holds a site engineer, a supervisor, a billing assistant and two more desks without feeling cramped. The door and window positions match the 20 x 8 ft plan, so the entry discipline stays the same.

variants.shortDescription: Thirty feet of length brings a second door, and that changes how the room works. Site staff enter at one end in boots, while visitors and clients use the other. Eight workstations line up, five along the rear wall and three along the front, with eight windows spreading daylight down the whole run. We keep this at eight desks rather than pushing to twelve, because a project office needs floor space for plan tables and standing conversations.

variants.shortDescription: This is the first layout with a partition. The first 10 ft becomes a private manager cabin with its own desk and two guest chairs, reached through an internal door. Behind it, a 30 ft common office runs seven workstations along one wall. Ten seats in total. At 8 ft of width the common room stays single-sided. Pick it when a closed meeting room matters more to you than want extra desks. An internal door keeps that room quiet.

variants.shortDescription: Ten feet of width lets both walls of the common office carry desks. Seven workstations sit along the rear wall and five along the front, which brings the total to twelve. Add the manager and two guest chairs and the cabin seats fifteen. The 10 ft manager room stays private behind the partition. Most infrastructure and EPC teams land here once the site crosses roughly forty people on the ground, and paperwork needs its own desks.

variants.shortDescription: The widest approved layout carries the same twelve workstations as the 40 x 10 ft plan. What you buy with the extra two feet is the aisle. Seven feet of clear floor runs between the two desk runs, so a plan table opens without anyone standing up. The manager cabin also gains width. Choose this when the office doubles as the daily coordination room rather than only a desk space. Both desk runs still take the standard 4 x 2.5 ft module.
